These are small learning experiments, each asking one question. Open a page
for an example, a comparison, and the recorded result. Details and runnable
code are available in a foldout.

Start with [adding six numbers](proofs/structure/attention-learns-fixed-width-sum.html),
[matching unfamiliar IDs](proofs/identity/unseen-identity-equality.html), or
[distinguishing missing values from zero](proofs/state/null-versus-zero.html).


Search by question, topic, result, or ID, such as `P021`.

::: {#proofs}
:::

<details>
<summary>How to read the results</summary>

These are experiments on synthetic data, not mathematical proofs or guarantees
for your dataset. A successful run can be provisional. Some experiments are
designed to demonstrate a limitation. Short execution checks, called smoke
runs, do not replace full learning results.

| Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| [Passing]{.proof-status data-proof-status="Passing"} | The latest full run meets its stated checks. |
| [Limited]{.proof-status data-proof-status="Limited"} | The experiment reproduces an expected limitation. |
| [Partial]{.proof-status data-proof-status="Partial"} | Part of the broader claim remains untested or inconsistent. |
| [Failing]{.proof-status data-proof-status="Failing"} | The latest full run misses at least one required check. |
| [Error]{.proof-status data-proof-status="Error"} | The latest full run could not complete. |
| [Missing]{.proof-status data-proof-status="Missing"} | No full run has been recorded. |

Each page shows selected measurements from its latest full run. Its history
can include repeated seeds and earlier source versions; the foldout and
[complete results](proofs/_generated/results.yaml) retain that context.
Experiments with more seeds provide stronger evidence about repeatability.

Learned arithmetic is approximate. Use
[preprocessing](guides/preprocessors.qmd) for business rules that require exact results.
Each page includes its reproduction command and a downloadable script.

</details>
